transcript:
Doctor: What brings you in today?
Patient: I have burning in my left heel.
Doctor: Did this start after your long shift yesterday?
Patient: At first I thought it started yesterday, but that was the day I changed shoes.
Doctor: When did the burning actually start?
Patient: I checked the calendar. It started four days ago.
Doctor: How bad is it now?
Patient: It is moderate.
Doctor: What have you taken for it?
Patient: I took acetaminophen before leaving home.
Doctor: Do you have any known allergies?
Patient: I have no known allergies.

Doctor: Before we begin, who needed the letter at the front desk?
Patient: My son needed the school letter. He is allergic to latex.
Doctor: Now tell me about your own reason for coming.
Patient: I have a dry cough.
Doctor: How long has your cough been going on?
Patient: For six days.
Doctor: What medicines have you tried for your cough?
Patient: I have not taken any medicine for it.
Doctor: Are you sure latex is also one of your allergies?
Patient: I do not know whether I have any allergies myself.
Doctor: Is the school letter part of your medical complaint?
Patient: The letter is for my son; my visit is for the cough.

medication.quote: I have not taken any medicine for it.

allergy.quote: I do not know whether I have any allergies myself.

transcript:
Doctor: How can we help today?
Patient: Please correct the mailing address on my receipt.
Doctor: Was it the receipt from a visit or from the pharmacy?
Patient: The visit. The receipt says ankle pain, but that was my sister's visit.
Doctor: Are you asking to change a treatment?
Patient: Only the mailing address needs changing.
Doctor: How long have you lived at the new address?
Patient: For eight months.
Doctor: Do you need a new copy of the letter as well?
Patient: Yes, please send the corrected receipt to the address on this form.

Doctor: What happened this morning?
Patient: I slipped on a step and my right wrist hurts.
Doctor: Is the warehouse where you work?
Patient: Yes. I was carrying a parcel for my shift.
Doctor: What number would you give the pain right now?
Patient: Seven out of ten was the number just after the fall.
Doctor: And now, while we are talking?
Patient: Right now it is three out of ten.
Doctor: Did you take any medicine for the wrist?
Patient: I cannot remember whether I took anything before the shift.
Doctor: Has a medicine ever caused an allergic reaction?
Patient: I am allergic to penicillin.

medication.quote: I cannot remember whether I took anything before the shift.

transcript:
Doctor: Tell me what brought you in.
Patient: I feel tingling in my fingertips.
Doctor: Did that begin when you started treatment?
Patient: I started the new tablets six weeks ago for something else.
Doctor: When did the tingling itself begin?
Patient: The tingling started two hours ago.
Doctor: Which tablets do you take?
Patient: I take metformin with breakfast.
Doctor: How would you describe the intensity of the tingling?
Patient: It is mild.
Doctor: Who reacted to the skin cream you mentioned to the nurse?
Patient: My roommate reacted to it. We did not discuss my own allergies.

Doctor: What problem are you experiencing?
Patient: I have swelling in my left ankle.
Doctor: The referral mentions a headache. Is that your complaint today?
Patient: That line belongs to my spouse's referral. I am here for my ankle.
Doctor: When did your ankle first swell?
Patient: I cannot tell when it began.
Doctor: What medicine have you used for it?
Patient: I thought I took naproxen.
Doctor: Is that still your answer after you checked the packet?
Patient: No, I was mistaken. I took ibuprofen.
Doctor: Do you know of any allergies?
Patient: No known allergies.

duration.quote: I cannot tell when it began.

transcript:
Receptionist: The video display is working again. Can you see the desk?
Patient: Yes, I can see the green folder now.
Doctor: Thanks for waiting. What brought you here?
Patient: My lips are burning.
Doctor: Is that the reason for this visit?
Patient: Yes. I first noticed it while putting my coat away.
Doctor: How long has that sensation been present?
Patient: It has been going on for three days.
Companion: I can move the laptop closer if that helps.
Doctor: What number describes the burning right now, from zero to ten?
Patient: Right now it is 2/10.
Doctor: Have you taken anything for it?
Patient: I took cetirizine.
Doctor: Is there an allergy to add to your records?
Patient: I have no allergies.

Receptionist: Is this about the copy desk or the health appointment?
Patient: The envelope from the copy desk arrived without the attachment.
Doctor: I can look up where it was mailed.
Companion: I had a headache for five days. That was my visit last month.
Patient: My companion is looking at a different envelope.
Doctor: Which paper did you expect?
Patient: The second page of the itemized bill.
Receptionist: The envelope number is in the top corner.
Patient: All I can see there is a blue stamp.
Doctor: Would you prefer the copy by mail?
Patient: Yes, the mailing address printed on the first page is correct.
Receptionist: I will mark this as a duplicate-page request.
Patient: Thanks, I can wait for the mail.

Doctor: The reception desk said two entries were copied into the wrong boxes.
Patient: I brought the little card with me to set things straight.
Companion: I can hold the card up to the light.
Doctor: Let's start with your own reason for coming today.
Patient: I have an itchy scalp.
Doctor: When did this begin?
Patient: I cannot remember when it started.
Doctor: What is on your allergy list? Please keep your medicines for the next question.
Patient: Nickel.
Doctor: Thanks. What medicines are you actually taking now?
Patient: No medications.
Doctor: Is the metal on the card difficult to read?
Patient: The type is tiny, but the word I just read is clear.
Companion: I can put the card away now.

duration.quote: I cannot remember when it started.

transcript:
Doctor: What symptom would you like me to record?
Patient: I have pain in my heel.
Doctor: I see two different numbers on the paper. Which one was from the weekend?
Patient: I wrote down 8/10 at the market on Saturday.
Companion: The pencil mark is faint in the photograph.
Doctor: Let's leave the old number on the paper. Check how the heel feels now.
Patient: I just stood on it again. The pain is 3/10 now.
Doctor: How long has this episode of heel pain lasted?
Patient: The heel pain has lasted eleven days.
Doctor: Did you take anything for it?
Patient: I took naproxen after lunch.
Companion: Would you like the original paper as well?
Doctor: The photograph is enough for today.
Patient: I will keep the original at home.

Doctor: Did the person beside you want to read their own appointment slip first?
Companion: Yes. I take loratadine, and my appointment is the one on Thursday.
Doctor: Thank you. Now I am speaking to the patient in the blue chair.
Patient: The chair is fine. My sister can stay and listen.
Doctor: What is bothering you yourself?
Patient: My fingers feel numb.
Doctor: Can you put a number on the numbness?
Patient: I am not sure how severe it is.
Companion: My own symptoms have lasted two months. Should I move my appointment?
Doctor: The desk can help you afterwards. Back to the person in the blue chair.
Doctor: Do you take any medications?
Patient: I do not take any medications.
Doctor: Is there anything about allergies to add to this form?
Patient: I do not know whether I have any allergies.
Companion: I will let the patient keep the page.

severity.quote: I am not sure how severe it is.

medication.quote: I do not take any medications.

allergy.quote: I do not know whether I have any allergies.

transcript:
Doctor: What brings you in today?
Patient: Left ankle swelling.
Doctor: How long has the swelling been there?
Patient: Four days.
Other: I was the one who picked you up after rehearsal. I still have the time in my calendar if we need it.
Patient: Give me a second to check the date of the rehearsal.
Other: Sorry, I was wrong about the pickup time. It was after lunch, not before lunch.
Patient: The swelling actually started two days ago. I had counted the wrong rehearsal.
Doctor: How bad is the swelling right now?
Patient: Moderate.
Doctor: What medicine did you take for it?
Patient: I took naproxen.
Doctor: Do you have any known allergies?
Patient: No known allergies.

Doctor: What brings you in today?
Patient: A dry cough.
Doctor: When did it start?
Patient: Six days ago.
Doctor: What medications are you using?
Patient: I take loratadine.
Doctor: Thanks. We'll come back to allergies after we go through your bag.
Unknown: I have the coatroom ticket. Shall I bring the bag into the room?
Other: There is a bottle of cetirizine in the bag, but that's my bottle. We brought both coats together.
Unknown: Sorry, I was mistaken. The bag is already here.
Patient: Yes, the bag is mine but that bottle isn't. I can read you my own label if you like.
Doctor: Any allergies you can confirm?
Patient: I don't know. My older records may have the answer.
Other: I can collect the folder on our way home.

Doctor: What would you like us to look at?
Patient: My hands shake.
Doctor: Can you tell me whether this began this week?
Patient: I haven't kept track. I don't know when it started.
Doctor: If zero is none and ten is the worst, how strong is it now?
Patient: I would say 7/10.
Patient: Wait, that was on the bus. Right now my shaking is 3/10.
Doctor: Thank you. Can someone help you lift the bag onto the chair?
Other: I'll put it by the window. I have a latex allergy, so I'd rather not wear those gloves myself.
Doctor: And do you take any medications?
Patient: No medications.
Doctor: Could you tell me your own allergies?
Patient: I am allergic to nickel.
Other: Your note for the metal bracelet is in that front pocket.

Doctor: What brings you in?
Patient: Ringing in my left ear.
Doctor: How long has the ringing lasted?
Patient: Three weeks.
Other: I can help with dates. We spent five days in the waiting room with my dad, and the ringing was there before that trip.
Doctor: Sorry, my question about the trip was unclear. I have the date for the ringing now.
Doctor: Which pain medicine did you use, if any?
Patient: I took aspirin.
Patient: Let me correct that. I did not take aspirin. I took ibuprofen.
Unknown: Your receipt for the parking fee is at the desk.
Doctor: Would you like to put a number on how bad the ringing is?
Patient: I can't put a number on it.
Doctor: Did anyone ever confirm an allergy for you?
Patient: I haven't checked yet.
